note: He matches the stated ICP on four of five criteria, including the one it names by name — the quote says prospects 'own their own business, or they're a physician', and this is a physician. Health is squarely the neglected area rather than a crisis: 15-20 lb gained to residency, no injuries, no conditions, seven hours of sleep. He is not deconditioned and not gym-averse — he has trained with kettlebells before and got results. Good-to-great holds: he is restoring a baseline he held eighteen months ago, not seeking rescue, and he set the bar himself at 175 lb and a 150 lb bench equivalent. He fails only on income, and only temporarily: 'the cost would have been an issue with one-on-one coaching. I'm not there yet. In a year, I would be.' This is the Badrane Hriouch pattern repeating — fits on profile, not on current willingness to pay, and the rep disqualified rather than discounted. The finding is that the stated ICP treats 'physician' and 'makes good money' as if they travel together, when a resident is a physician on a trainee salary. Either the ICP needs a career-stage qualifier, or residents belong in a diarised pipeline rather than a loss column.
